method.registry_probe: GET https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=<token>&limit=100 per token, curl -s -m 15, FULLY paginated by following metadata.nextCursor until null (fixes the single-page-undercount mistake a prior round was burned by). All 30 tokens in this round resolved on page 1 with nextCursor null, so metadata.count is confirmed as the true total, not a first-page undercount.
method.scoring: Identical to round 13: empty_slot_score = 100/(1+count); fit (0-1) = pairing with the current server suite; buildability (0-1) = pure-TypeScript/local-files/no-network/no-paid-API feasibility gate; score = empty_slot_score x fit x buildability. Scale and weights unchanged from data/intel_r13.json so round 14 is directly comparable to round 13.
method.build_gate: build only if count < 20 AND fit > 0.6 AND buildability > 0.7 (same gate as round 13)

dedup_note: Built a 239-token exclusion set from every bold/table-row token in all prior INTEL_R*/NAMING_R*_RESULT files, plus a live registry check against every already-published io.github.theluckystrike/* variant name found in data/distribution.json's per_server registry-name notes. Two candidates were dropped after colliding with variants published THIS SAME LOOP for the round-13 change-order and round-'amortization' builds (variation-order and scope-change already resolve to our own change-order row; lease-schedule already resolves to our own amortization row) and replaced with retention-money and labour-burden before scoring.

tokens_probed.note: Debit note generator, the debit side of R12/R13's existing credit-note pairing; adjacent to invoice, billing-docs, statement-of-account. Same doc-template shape as invoice/billing-docs, no network.
SOW / scope-of-work document: engagement scope, deliverables, assumptions, exclusions, sign-off. Strong adjacency to clauses and quotes (reuses clause-library and PDF export shape).

Per-job cost roll-up: labour (from time-tracker-shaped entries), materials (from catalogue), overhead allocation, budget-vs-actual. Reads across work-order/time-tracker/catalogue -- a genuine seam server, moderately complex allocation math.
Interim/progress payment claim against a contract value: percent complete, amount previously certified, retention withheld, amount now due. Adjacent to change-order/quotes/invoice.
Bill-of-materials / materials list for a job: item, quantity, unit, supplier reference, cost from catalogue. Adjacent to work-order and catalogue.

Construction retention/retainage held back per contract and its release schedule. Adjacent to change-order, work-order and invoice; distinct job from recurring's 'retainer' variant (subscription billing, not held-back money).

Plant/equipment hire tracker: third-party hired-in plant, hire cost per day/week, off-hire date, cost roll-up. Distinct from R13's equipment-loan (internal asset checkout) -- this is external hire cost. Adjacent to asset-register/catalogue.
Daywork sheet: time-and-materials record for variation work billed at day rates plus a percentage addition, the UK trades term. Adjacent to work-order/time-tracker.
Practical completion / certificate of completion: formal handover document referencing outstanding defects and triggering retention release. Adjacent to work-order, change-order, catalogue.
Fully-loaded labour cost rate calculator: wage plus burden percentage (taxes, insurance, overhead) to a true hourly cost. Adjacent to job-costing/time-tracker/catalogue's role rates.
Daily site diary: weather, crew on site, plant on site, visitors, progress note, one row per day. Adjacent to work-order.
Cost-plus contract billing: fee equals actual costs plus a markup percentage, reconciliation of billed vs actual. Adjacent to invoice/quotes/job-costing.
Cost-code / WBS-style coding structure for allocating spend to a job. More a taxonomy than a document generator, so buildability discounted for being thin as a standalone tool.
Defects-liability-period tracker: the time-bound warranty window after handover and its retention-release trigger, distinct from the defect LIST itself (already R12's snagging/punch-list).
Self-billing invoice arrangement where the buyer issues the invoice on the supplier's behalf. Adjacent to invoice/recurring; jurisdiction-specific VAT self-billing rules add real correctness risk.
Same job as progress-claim under the US billing term; fit capped for near-total overlap with progress-claim rather than opening a second empty slot.
Day-rate contract calculator: rate x days with partial-day and expense adjustments. Adjacent to time-tracker/quotes but thin as a standalone product.
Call-off order drawing down quantity/value against a pre-agreed framework agreement over time. Adjacent to work-order/quotes/catalogue; framework-agreement concept adds scope complexity.

Extension-of-time (EOT) construction claim: schedule delay days claimed against a cause, days awarded. Adjacent to change-order/work-order but fundamentally a schedule/legal claim, less numeric than the rest of the fleet.
Billable-vs-available utilisation percentage report. Thin -- largely a report computed from time-tracker's own data rather than a standalone store, so fit and buildability both discounted.
Same retention-holdback job as retainage under a different name; fit capped for near-duplication rather than a second empty slot.
Unit price / cost-per-unit lookup; catalogue already stores dated unit prices by SKU and role. Fit capped for overlap with the existing catalogue server.

Mechanic's-lien waiver document, a US construction legal form. Buildability discounted: the statutory waiver wording differs by US state, so an honest one-round build cannot claim jurisdiction-correct output.

Subcontractor management -- ambiguous scope (could mean agreement, payment tracking, insurance/compliance tracking); buildability discounted for the same generic/ambiguous pattern R13 flagged on 'variation'/'overrun'.
Safety toolbox-talk record-keeping. Off-thesis (safety/compliance rather than back-office finance/docs), same pattern R13 scored low for near-miss/risk-register.
Labour-hours-on-a-job log; overlaps time-tracker (hours) and work-order's own labour lines. Fit capped for overlap.
Near-synonym of work-order; work-order already registered a 'job-card' registry variant covering this exact job. Scored but heavily fit-capped as a duplicate, not a fresh slot.
Generic construction daily report; 3 real competitors on the registry already and conceptually overlaps site-diary.

UK lease-end dilapidations/reinstatement-cost claim. Off-thesis (property/lease surveying, not core back-office); buildability discounted -- a genuine dilapidations assessment needs surveyor judgement no local-file tool can honestly automate.

Construction quantity takeoff/estimating from drawings. 57 real competitors (construction-takeoff-estimating, opentakeoff) confirm real demand, but buildability is low: an honest takeoff tool needs drawing/plan parsing, not a fit for a local-files-only stdio server in one round.

part2_marginal_server_verdict.question: Given 30-31 servers, 83 registry manifests, and a measured ~50% registry findability ceiling, is building server #31/32/33 still the best use of a build round?
part2_marginal_server_verdict.verdict: NO -- the marginal server is not paying for itself on any measured signal. The build round should shift to fixing conversion and distribution on the existing 31 servers rather than adding a 32nd/33rd.
part2_marginal_server_verdict.build_order_evidence: First-commit timestamps for servers/<name>/ via git log --diff-filter=A --follow: cash-book 2026-09-06T02:31:55+07:00, amortization 05:06:28, petty-cash 07:39:00, work-order 10:10:23, catalogue 12:46:30, change-order 14:27:17 -- all same day, ordered by commit time.

measured_findings.evidence: data/kpi.json 2026-09-06: Checkout sessions from humans (last 100) = 68, Paid sessions = 0, License keys minted = 0, Pro tenants on hosted endpoints = 0. Revenue from the newest 5 specifically cannot be more than the estate total of $0.

curl -A '<Chrome UA>' -D - https://mcp.zovo.one/buy/<id> for all 5: amortization and petty-cash return 303 to a live checkout.stripe.com session; work-order, catalogue and change-order (3 of the last 5, 60%) return HTTP 503 with header x-mcp-buy: price-pending-human -- the Pro tier of the majority of the newest servers cannot even be bought right now, human step required.

All 5 are live at v0.20.0 on their bare name (amortization rank1/5, petty-cash rank1/4, work-order rank1/3, catalogue rank11/14 i.e. p=0.91, change-order rank1/1). All 5 also carry 1-2 published compound-slug registry-name variants (loan-schedule, cash-float, imprest-account, job-card, price-list, rate-card, variation-order, scope-change) that resolve ONLY to our own row (self-created slugs, tautological rank1). None of this proves a real buyer's actual search reaches us: data/organic.json's own documented search_semantics states any two-word query WITH A SPACE returns 0 results fleet-wide, and generic single words that people really type (e.g. 'price', 'loan', 'job') are swamped (price alone: our older price-tracker ranks 106th of 131). A 32nd/33rd server inherits the identical structural ceiling.
measured_findings.source: measured 2026-09-07, registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=<token>&limit=100 for the 5 servers' own names + 10 planned variant slugs; data/organic.json search_semantics

measured_findings.signal: Tracked in the fleet's own findability model
measured_findings.evidence: data/organic.json's servers[] list (the file that computes the fleet's organic/findable score) does not contain amortization, petty-cash, work-order, catalogue or change-order at all -- it was last generated 2026-09-06 against an earlier server set. The estate's only findability instrument has never measured whether the last 5 builds clear the ~50% ceiling.

All 5 ARE submitted: Docker MCP catalog PR #4892 body lists all 5 by name (30 servers total in that PR), but the PR has 1 general comment, 0 review comments, and mergeable_state=blocked, unchanged in engagement pattern from every prior round. Cline marketplace has 5 open issues (one per server, #2455/2458/2459/2460/2461), each with 0 comments. Smithery and Glama show 0 presence for the whole estate (re-confirmed pattern, not specific to these 5). The one real high-traffic directory in progress, awesome-mcp-servers PR #13473, is CI-blocked on a Glama listing that has not happened, and does not include any of these 5 at all.

All 5 have a live /s/<id> page in the sitemap and a health-endpoint product entry, same as every other server. No per-server traffic instrument exists anywhere in this repo (data/metrics.json and data/distribution.json record download counts and submission status, not page views); the estate-wide traffic proxy (GitHub views/uniques/clones) was measured flat at 0 in the last organic.json pass. Bundle downloads for the 5 newest sum to roughly 8 (change-order, 1 release old) to 37 (amortization, present in 5 releases) via gh api releases asset download_count -- small numbers, same zero-to-sale conversion the rest of the 31-server estate has shown since day one.

what_would_pay_better: Fix the 3 broken Pro checkouts (work-order, catalogue, change-order 503 price-pending-human) -- this converts EXISTING traffic/downloads immediately, at near-zero build cost, versus a 32nd server that inherits the same broken-checkout risk pattern.

Get Glama listed (the one hard blocker named in every awesome-mcp-servers PR round since #13473 opened) -- that single unblock reaches a 2,237+-entry real directory with real traffic for ALL 31 servers at once, which is a bigger distribution lever than any single new server.

Add amortization/petty-cash/work-order/catalogue/change-order to data/organic.json's tracked query_set so the estate's own findability model actually measures the newest third of the catalogue instead of scoring it blind.

Spend the round on one real outreach action that produces the estate's first sale (a real human touchpoint on the Docker/Cline PRs sitting at 0 comments for weeks, or a backlink from a site with actual traffic) rather than a document generator nobody outside this repo has seen yet.
